author: Shajaka Shelton
title: Man sentenced for 2022 false signature election fraud scheme - NewsBreak
text:
By Shajaka Shelton ,
2 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — A Michigan man convicted of defrauding multiple 2022 state political campaigns of thousands of dollars in a false signature scheme that saw multiple candidates disqualified from the ballot was sentenced to four to 20 years in prison Wednesday.
“Died prior to the date of signing”: Report finds 68,000 invalid signatures Shawn Wilmoth, of Warren, is one of three men originally charged in 2023 with defrauding multiple political campaigns out of nearly $400,000 after delivering them false signatures, according to Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel. Wilmoth and co-conspirator Willie Reed, of Pompano Beach, FL, were found guilty of multiple felonies back in February.
A third defendant, Jamie Wilmoth-Goodin, of Warren, was found not guilty.
Six gubernatorial candidates — Ryan Kelley, Perry Johnson, James Craig, Donna Brandenburg, Michael Brown, and Michael Markey — and three judicial candidates — Tricia Dare, John Cahalan, and John Michael Malone — contracted with Wilmouth and Reed for the purposes of fulfilling their nomination signature requirements.
These candidates needed 15,000 signatures to appear on the ballot for the August 2022 primary election. However, Wilmoth and Reed instead delivered “tens of thousands” of forged signatures to the campaigns, Nessel said.
The state flagged the signatures in May 22 due to evidence of “round-tabling,” where a group of individuals take turn signing one line on each signature sheet in an attempt to pass the handwriting off as authentic.
Seven of these candidates ultimately failed to meet the state’s signature requirements to appear on the ballot. Brown did not submit his signatures for review and withdrew following a report from the state exposing the other candidates for submitting fraudulent signatures. Kelley did not receive any signatures at all.
In February, Wilmoth was convicted of 22 charges, including:
1 count, Conducting a Criminal Enterprise 2 counts, False Pretenses, $100,000 or more 2 counts, False Pretenses, $50,000 to $100,000 3 counts, False Pretenses, $20,000 to $50,000 7 counts, Use of a Computer to Commit a Crime, $20,000 or more 7 counts, Election Law Forgery. Reed was found guilty of 12 charges, including conducting a criminal enterprise, false pretenses and election law forgery. His sentencing is set for March 31.
